correctness.rationale: The repaired RESULT keeps the valid proof. Admissible disjoint downset/upset pairs are realized by the extension property and determine the complete type by homogeneity. The empty-side cases count 2i(G)-1; nonempty pairs across the bipartition are independent sets meeting both sides in the bipartite complement. Padding multiplies the original i(G) by 2^k, and the complement gains exactly (2^k-1)2^a independent sets using the new side vertices. The unchanged remainder has -1<=Delta<2^k, so the floor with +1 extracts i(G) exactly. A disjoint edge if needed multiplies the source answer by three and keeps a comparability after padding, ensuring exact height two even for edge-free inputs. One checked ternary labeling per nonalgebraic type and a tagged choice per equality type give the two #P memberships. Height one has only the empty-side cases. Bit lengths and the instance size are linear in the vertex count apart from explicit relation encoding.
residual_risks: No parsimonious reduction, approximation claim, or preservation of connectedness or bounded degree is established.

The replacement identifies the identity as prior and narrows the contribution to one-query extraction from an absolute type count at exact height two. The matched local reduction has a one-query oracle for a shifted difference of two counts, not for the absolute count; the older result for posets with a greatest element uses two queries and does not retain the height promise. Neither inspected argument supplies this absolute one-query extraction.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem separates height one from height two for a natural complete-type counting problem and shows that the harder case needs only one absolute evaluation in a reduction. Independent-set hardness of the absolute count does not follow merely because the count contains independent-set terms. The isolated-side padding addresses that obstacle without increasing poset height, and is the substantive contribution rather than the reused counting identity.
residual_risks: The result concerns exact counting in an explicitly named finite parameter poset only.
